source.title: Selective Memory Retention for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

assessments.primary_source_quality: Useful primary study with a frozen action model, explicit bounded-retention policies, two-seed clean evaluation, a controlled 75% noisy-write stress, task-success and retrieval metrics, and held-out in-distribution evaluation. It is single-author, recent, code reproducibility was not confirmed in this pass, and no independent replication was identified.
assessments.quantitative_result: On clean ALFWorld with gpt-5-mini, external memory improves over no memory but bounded-policy differences remain within Wilson 95% confidence intervals for T=100-200. Under 75% synthetic distractor writes, unbounded memory Precision@5 falls 20.2%→12.4% and FIFO-K50 15.8%→3.8%, while TraceRetain-CEM stays about 16.9%→16.6% and preserves 97/100 task success. Held-out in-distribution memory policies solve 47-49/50 tasks versus 39/50 for no memory.
assessments.matched_baseline: Strong for the evaluation-design premise: clean versus deliberately polluted memory streams are compared, and several retention policies are run under the same stress. Two seeds and one benchmark/model limit precision/generalization.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderately strong for the claim that a retention mechanism intended to resist pollution must be tested under actual pollution pressure, because clean saturated tasks do not discriminate policies while controlled noise does. Less strong for the exact O stress mixture of failed traces, superseded facts, irrelevant observations and redundant successes, which is a transfer design.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: No official repository was confirmed by the source worker in this run; primary arXiv abstract verifies the central stress result.
assessments.failure_evidence: Directly shows a clean benchmark can yield a misleading null between bounded retention strategies when the failure mode they target is absent.
scope_limits: Single-author study, ALFWorld, gpt-5-mini and synthetic 75% distractor writes.
Precision@5 is not identical to downstream decision quality, though 97/100 task success supplies an action-level outcome in the stress setting.
Stress composition/rate matters; one noise regime should not become a universal retention benchmark.
The clean-policy null is scoped to low-pollution saturation, not evidence that retention policies are equivalent.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B+ for controlled pollution stress revealing retention-policy differences in the tested setting.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C+/B- for an O memory-pollution stress suite until its injected failure distribution is justified and downstream O decisions are measured.

source.title: ActionEngine: From Reactive to Programmatic GUI Agents via State Machine Memory

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong primary system paper for repeated GUI interaction: crawler-validated state-machine memory, executable-program synthesis, local re-grounding/repair, end-to-end success, LLM-call, cost and latency metrics. No independent replication identified and transfer beyond GUI is not established.
assessments.quantitative_result: On Reddit tasks from WebArena, ActionEngine reports 95% task success with on average one LLM call versus 66% for the strongest vision-only baseline, while reducing cost by 11.8x and end-to-end latency by 2x.
assessments.matched_baseline: Useful native-domain baseline and direct end-to-end metrics. The O proposal specifically compares full reasoning every repeat versus a typed validated template plus local repair after one validated run; that exact one-shot compile/reuse protocol is not isolated in the source.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Strong for programmatic execution from prevalidated GUI state-machine memory in the tested WebArena subset; weak-to-moderate for transfer to repeated O procedures with heterogeneous tools and semantics.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: No official ActionEngine repository was confirmed by the source worker; primary abstract verifies the headline mechanism and metrics.
assessments.failure_evidence: Supports the premise that repeated reactive LLM reasoning can be unnecessarily expensive and error-prone when environment transition structure is stable enough to prevalidate and compile.
scope_limits: GUI/WebArena Reddit tasks benefit from stable interface structure; novel research/engineering tasks may be less compilable.
Stale templates need explicit version/freshness validation.
Localized visual re-grounding is domain-specific and does not specify O's fallback mechanism.
The worker's O experiment is a transfer hypothesis, not evidence that O currently has a repeatable compilable task family with similar gains.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B+ for ActionEngine in its native GUI setting.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C for compiling validated O procedures until a matched repeated-task family shows end-to-end benefit with stale-template/fallback controls.

source.title: NetAgentBench: A State-Centric Benchmark for Evaluating Agentic Network Configuration

assessments.primary_source_quality: Useful primary benchmark paper with finite-state-machine task formalization designed for deterministic correctness and bounded execution, plus empirical evaluation of four contemporary LLM agents. It is network-configuration-specific and does not establish an intervention/recovery policy.
assessments.quantitative_result: The source reports that four state-of-the-art agents can solve basic configurations but show severe exploration meltdowns and coherence collapse on expert-level multi-turn configurations. The abstract establishes the qualitative state-centric failure pattern but does not expose enough exact per-agent numeric deltas for a higher quantitative grade in this pass.
assessments.matched_baseline: Moderate. Basic-versus-expert task difficulty and deterministic state transitions reveal where behavior becomes incoherent, but the proposed O state-transition metric is not compared against prose-only progress monitoring on matched O runs.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderate for state-centric evaluation as a diagnostic framework; low for claiming it predicts or prevents O failures better than existing O source-bound state observations.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: FSM formalization is explicit in the source; no independent execution performed here.
assessments.failure_evidence: Supports the importance of authoritative state transitions and bounded behavioral stability checks instead of trusting terminal prose alone.
scope_limits: No particular anomaly detector, recovery rule or threshold is validated.
Qualitative 'meltdown/coherence collapse' claims need exact full-text metrics before grading a specific detector highly.
O already contains source/state binding machinery, so literature support for state-centric evaluation is distinct from evidence that a new O metric adds value.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B for deterministic FSM state-centric benchmarking in the tested network domain.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C+/B- for adding a new O state-transition trace metric until it demonstrates incremental held-out diagnostic or outcome value over existing source-bound state tracking.

cross_source_synthesis: TraceRetain is especially valuable as evidence about benchmark design: a mechanism can look indistinguishable on clean saturated workloads because its target failure mode is absent, so negative conclusions must be conditioned on stress coverage.

ActionEngine gives strong native-domain evidence for moving stable repeated work out of the reasoning loop, but its transfer to O is substantially weaker than the 95%/11.8x/2x GUI result might suggest.
NetAgentBench supports authoritative state-centric diagnostics but does not by itself justify a new recovery mechanism or prove incremental value over O's existing state-binding controls.
